articles.title: Brewers parade to celebrate 2026 World Series title set for Friday
articles.summary: The Brewers clinched the first World Series in franchise history on Wednesday night against the Rays.
articles.body:
Milwaukee will get its first sports championship-related parade since 2021 on Friday when the Brewers celebrate their 2026 World Series title.

Five years after the Bucks delivered an NBA championship, the Brewers and their fans will have their opportunity to continue to revel in the team's first World Series title (and the city's second after the 1957 Braves) with a Parade of Champions beginning at 11 a.m. ET.

Two days after the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to clinch the series in Game 5, the Commissioner's Trophy will be in attendance as the festivities are set to run through downtown Milwaukee and conclude at Henry Maier Festival Park.

During his postgame press conference, Brewers manager Pat Murphy jokingly asked two of his sons, Austin and Jaxon, whether their little league baseball duties might interfere with attending the parade.

Pat, Austin and Jaxon will be joined by team alumni during the festivities. There will also be a special showing of "Ueck," the documentary about legendary Brewers broadcaster Bob Uecker.

There will also be a Championship Rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater inside the park.

Should some fans be unable to attend, the parade will be streamed on MLB Network, MLB and Brewers.com.

articles.title: 2026 MLB Free Agents Rumors, Predictions for Tarik Skubal, Brandon Lowe, More
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are your 2026 World Series champions, which can only mean one thing.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are your 2026 World Series champions, which can only mean one thing.

The MLB offseason has officially arrived.

The Brewers might be celebrating still, and the Tampa Bay Rays have joined a few different teams at various stages of the grief process, but all 30 front offices have reached roster-building time.

So, let's put a spotlight on some possible roster-building manuevers and dig into the latest buzz around baseball's free agents.

The Pittsburgh Pirates' trade for Brandon Lowe last offseason could not have gone any better. In fact, you could argue it went a little too well, since his offensive production (35 homers, 96 RBI) and defensive improvement seemingly positioned him for the kind of pay raise that could price out Pittsburgh.

If that was the fear for Pirates fans, a recent contract projection from The Athletic's Jim Bowden (a former MLB executive) landed lower than expected: three years, $45 million. Bowden also listed the Pirates as one of Lowe's three best team fits, along with the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres.

If that's all it takes to get Lowe's signature on the dotted line, the Pirates should be ready to pounce. He's had some availability issues in his past, but if those are behind him (284 games played the past two seasons), a new contract could be heavy on rewards and light on risks.

That just doesn't seem like it will be enough—in annual salary, or in years. And if his actual contract value climbs higher, it probably will force a departure from Pittsburgh and steer him toward a deeper-pocketed club with an opening on the infield.

Prediction: Lowe signs with the New York Yankees.

For all of the unknowns in this MLB offseason, the clearest certainty is that a colossal contract (very possibly a record-setting one) is coming Tarik Skubal's way.

He isn't necessarily a perfect free agent, what with his 30th birthday fast approaching and the fact he had to navigate around elbow surgery this season. That said, his previous two campaigns featured Cy Young awards, and this one showed similar dominance ( 2.51 FIP this year; 2.45 and 2.49 in 2025 and 2024, respectively).

He'll send this market in a frenzy. Every big-spender—starting with the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—will at least weigh making a bid, and surprise suitors could surface, too. That said, cold water is already getting dumped on the idea of Skubal heading back to the Detroit Tigers.

"It's probably too early to handicap this as Mets versus Dodgers," ESPN's Alden Gonzalez wrote. "... Others will surely step up—though it seems highly unlikely that the Tigers, who never made an extension offer Skubal's side deemed competitive, will be among them."

While that would have been a fun way for this story to end, it never felt too feasible. Because, in all likelihood, it probably isn't too early to consider this a two-team race between New York and L.A.

Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Chicago Cubs knew they were headed for a busy offseason given the number of free agents on their roster, but they just had even more business added to their to-do list.

Per ESPN's Jesse Rogers , Clay Holmes and Matthew Boyd will both decline options to enter free agency. They'll also see a lot of familiar faces from this rotation when they get there, since Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman and David Peterson are on the open market as well.

Holmes, acquired in a trade deadline deal with the New York Mets, pitched to a 3.29 ERA over 101.1 innings split between the teams. Boyd, meanwhile, had a 3.91 ERA and 1.21 WHIP in his 126.2 innings.

Of the five pitchers listed above, Rogers opined that one or two "could return." That feels about right, since the Cubs need to upgrade their rotation while also addressing other holes on the roster.

Prediction: Holmes and Peterson re-sign with the Cubs.

articles.title: Important 2026-2027 offseason dates
articles.summary: Look for a lot of activity in November.
articles.body:
With 2026 baseball officially behind us, and so much speculation and insecurity around 2027 baseball, we are now entering that liminal space between seasons that may wind up lasting far longer than any of us would like. We will be with you throughout all of it, however long it lasts, and to begin the official offseason coverage, we're going to take a look at some important dates for the Mets and Major League Baseball as a whole.

At the end of the season, the Mets had zero (0) free agents. Every single player that was due to hit free agency today was traded (or claimed off waivers) during the season. And so the 9am deadline came and went without any Mets activity at all.

In terms of the internal machinations, the Mets have no Qualifying Offers to issue. The Mets currently have three players on the 60-day Injured List who will need to rejoin the 40-Man roster (Tylor Megill, Reed Garrett, and Jorge Polanco). Bo Bichette is the only Met with a player option, so he will have to make a decision about his future in Queens by Monday evening.

With the lockout expected to begin less than a month from now, look for free agency to happen quite quickly.

These are usually fairly tame, in terms of trades and signings, compared to the Winter Meetings, but with those in question, look for the GM meetings to be a hotbed of activity.

Deadline for players to accept the Qualifying Offer, 4 pm ET

Rule 5 protection deadline (Players need to be added to 40-man roster to protect from the Rule 5 draft)

With the Mets needing to add some minor leaguers to their 40-man roster, expect a flurry of releases and trades to make some room before this deadline. Our Lukas Vlahos did a great job of outlining where the Mets' roster stands at the end of the season.

Expect to see a lot of cigars lit with $100 bills and other signs of excess while crying poverty.

See the note about the Rule 5 deadline above.

CBA Expires 11:59 pm ET – Lockout begins

This is the big one; even if things go better than any of us expect, there will likely still be a lockout starting on December 1st.

December 7-9 : Winter Meetings in San Diego

January 8 : Arbitration Figures Exchanged

The Winter Meetings almost certainly won't happen, and the others in this category will be postponed until the lockout ends.

This will be the only real activity between the lockout's beginning and end.

The Mets have three players – Luis Torrens, Nolan McLean, and Carson Benge – who are Gold Glove finalists. The award announcements will be exclusively revealed via ESPN at 9pm EST.

HOF eight-person Contemporary Baseball Era ballot for managers, executives and umpires Silver Slugger Award finalists announced – 2 pm ET

The Mets look to have at least one Rookie of the Year candidate, but seem unlikely have any finalists in any other categories (Cy Young, MVP, Manager of the Year). These will be announced on an MLB Network broadcast from 6pm-8pm.

Heart & Hustle Awards announced – TBD – MLB Network Gold Glove Awards dinner in NYC – Platinum Glove winners announced

Rookie of the Year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

It seems likely that Carson Benge and/or Nolan McLean get votes in the Rookie of the Year category, with Benge being the Met frontrunner.

Manager of the Year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

The Mets had two managers this year and neither seems likely to grab any votes here.

Cy Young Awards and BBWAA relievers of year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

MLB Awards show – 9-11pm ET (MLB Network)

Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman relievers of year Edgard Martinez DH of year

I suppose there is a chance that a Met picks up an honor on the first or second team, but that seems like the only likely Mets action here.

In what world would a 2026 Mets be an MVP candidate?

Hall of Fame announces its 2027 ballot, 12 pm ET – Writer's ballot

Bobby Abreu, David Wright, and Francisco Rodriguez will all be on this ballot, with potential ex-Mets Asdrubal Cabrera, Todd Frazier, and Jay Bruce potentially looking at debuts on the ballot.

BBWAA announces Contemporary Baseball Era inductees

Hall of Fame announces BBWAA voting results & 2007 inductees, 6 p ET (MLB Network)

articles.title: Dominican Appeals Court Revokes Wander Franco Pardon in Sex Abuse Case
articles.summary: SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic (AP) — An appeals court in the Dominican Republic on Thursday granted a request by prosecutors to revoke a judicial pardon previously awarded to Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.
articles.body:
SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic (AP) — An appeals court in the Dominican Republic on Thursday granted a request by prosecutors to revoke a judicial pardon previously awarded to Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.

The Dominican Public Prosecutor's Office argued that the lower court's original pardon rested on an erroneous interpretation of legal provisions intended only for exceptional circumstances — conditions that prosecutors maintained do not apply to Franco's case.

Franco's defense team objected to the motion, but the appellate court ruled in favor of the prosecution, essentially upholding Franco's previous conviction, with a suspended three-year prison sentence. Franco will not be required to serve time in custody provided he maintains a fixed residence and remains under judicial supervision.

Franco was arrested in January 2024 after being accused of having a four-month relationship with a girl who was 14 at the time and transferring thousands of dollars to her mother to consent to the illegal relationship . Franco, now 25, was originally convicted in June of 2025.

Six months after that, Tampa Bay placed him on the restricted list, which cut off the pay he had been receiving while on administrative leave. He hasn't played in the majors since. Tampa Bay was eliminated from the World Series last night by the Milwaukee Brewers.

The court on Thursday imposed the conditional terms considering Franco's age and to support his eventual reintegration into society. If he fails to comply with any of the conditions, he will be required to serve the full three-year prison sentence.

Neither Franco nor his legal counsel offered statements to the press upon leaving the courthouse.

Franco, who was once the Ray's star shortstop, had signed a $182 million, 11-year contract in November 2021 but saw his career abruptly halted in August 2023 after authorities in the Dominican Republic announced they were investigating him for an alleged relationship with a minor. Franco was 22 at the time.

Following Thursday's hearing, prosecutors reiterated that they had substantiated their charges throughout multiple trials, presenting robust evidence that established the criminal conduct of both Franco and the minor's mother.

The court upheld a 10-year prison sentence for the mother, who was found guilty of commercial sexual exploitation and money laundering.

Additionally, the court ordered the forfeiture of approximately $34,000 found in her possession — funds provided by Franco in exchange for her consent to his relationship with her daughter.

Franco retains the right to appeal this decision to the Supreme Court of Justice of the Dominican Republic.

Major League Baseball declined to comment.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers broke baseball on their way to remarkably dominant World Series run
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers went 11-2 in the postseason and never trailed in a series, but their dominant World Series run reveals a truth about baseball.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers are 2026 World Series champions, bringing home the organization's first ever title. For the franchise and their fans, it was the culmination of years of quality scouting, drafting, international signings, player development, and remarkably successful trades. It was also a near-perfect example of what it takes to win a championship in baseball. While William Contreras won World Series MVP, voters had plenty of options to choose from on the Milwaukee roster. Jackson Chourio became the first player since Babe Ruth, yes, literally Babe Ruth, to have 10 hits in the first four games of a World Series. Cooper Pratt, a light-hitting, defense-first shortstop, set a rookie record with hits in six straight at bats from game four to game five. BREWERS RIDE RIDICULOUS, RECORD-SETTING EIGHT-RUN INNING TO DOMINANT 3-0 WORLD SERIES LEAD OVER RAYS Brice Turang hit .316, below average hitter David Hamilton crushed what looked like a huge home run in game four. Aaron Ashby went 5.2 innings with no runs, just one hit allowed and nine strikeouts. Abner Uribe allowed just two hits in 5 innings. Jacob Misiorowski allowed only one run in 10.2 innings, winning game one and the clinching game five. Robert Gasser was equally unhittable, with just one run allowed in his game three start. A start so incredible that it was the first of its type by a left-handed pitcher since legendary Hall of Famer Sandy Koufax. The whole team was World Series MVP. The whole team was NLCS MVP, and NLDS MVP too. Milwaukee went 11-2 in the postseason against the San Diego Padres, the hottest team in baseball in the second half, the star-studded 100-win Los Angeles Dodgers, and the 98-win Tampa Bay Rays, who tore through the American League. They won eight straight games in the playoffs. Their two losses came by a combined two runs, and their one World Series loss was on a walk-off in the 12th inning after they blew a 3-2 lead. It's not a stretch to say it's one of the most dominant stretches of playoff baseball in the history of the sport. And it's why we can make the argument that the Milwaukee Brewers broke Major League Baseball. It's not supposed to be this easy, and it rarely is, even for some of the most expensive, talented rosters we've ever seen. The 2024 Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani coming off the first 50-50 season in history and a long list of other stars, were down 2-1 in the NLDS to the Padres before coming back to win. It took them six games to beat the Mets in the NLCS. They very nearly lost the clinching game five of the World Series, falling behind 5-0 to the Yankees before the New York defense went on a comical run of errors and mental mistakes. In 2025, they were down to their final two outs in game seven of the series against Toronto, until Miguel Rojas hit a miraculous game-tying homer. Milwaukee? They never trailed in a series, or even came close. In fact, it was the exact opposite. They had a 2-0 lead in the NLDS, a 4-0 lead in the NLCS, and a 3-0 lead in the NLCS. It's remarkable. Which raises the question, how did they do it? What was their philosophy and approach in October? The real answer, boring as it might be, they didn't do anything. Baseball happened. That's not to say that the Brewers don't have good players or didn't have good results. Misiorowski is going to win the Cy Young Award at 24-years-old, and looks set to dominate the league for years to come. Christian Yelich is a former MVP, multiple-time Silver Slugger Award winner and borderline candidate for the Hall of Fame. William Contreras has been a top-three catcher in baseball for several years. Garrett Mitchell is a former first round pick and top prospect, as is Brice Turang. Jackson Chourio is already a star at 22. The big secret the Brewers discovered? Have your players get hot at the right time, have a few bounces go your way, rely on some of your less talented players to hit perfectly timed home runs, and sit back and watch as your bullpen goes from very good to almost literally untouchable. Every year, the greater baseball world looks to find some sort of meaning or blueprint from the team that wins the World Series. In 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers "proved" that you can just guarantee a title by spending money, even though the Mets and Yankees haven't won in decades. In 2023, the Rangers showed you need a veteran manager like Bruce Bochy, and that home runs, Texas hit eight in five games, are how you win in October. Very smart analysts have pointed to quality bullpens, big midseason trades, drafting and development, free agency, dominant starting rotations, home runs, or making contact and putting the ball in play. The reality? You need all of those, and you can't predict which ones you'll actually get when it matters. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Not once in these discussions does anyone acknowledge that the different paths taken by different teams demonstrate that there is no one way to win a championship. And that the disparate approaches to roster construction show that what actually matters is a combination of timing, randomness, luck, and talent. Because there has to be meaning and lessons and broad conclusions to draw from every outcome, the baseball world picks a reason and explanation, then quietly discards it when next year's team does the opposite. Here are a few examples of why looking for meaning in playoff baseball is pointless. "Clutch" hitting is frequently praised as meaningful and predictive. Some players just have the "clutch" gene, the received baseball wisdom goes. So let's look at superstar shorstop Corey Seager as an example. Seager had an astonishing run in the 2020 playoffs, hitting. 328 with eight home runs and 20 runs batted in, winning NLCS and World Series MVP. One of the best postseasons ever. Clutch hitter, right? In 2016 and 2017, he went a combined 18 for 82. Then in the 2019 postseason went 3-20 with two singles and no homers. In 2021, Seager was 9-48, a .188 batting average. In 2023, he was once again a force of nature for Texas, hitting .318 with six homers. So is Seager the clutch playoff force from 2020 and 2023, or the hopeless, unclutch, "moment is too big" failure from 2016, 2017, 2019, and 2021? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Therein lies the problem. Corey Seager is an elite hitter, but even the best hitters go through hot and cold streaks. Pitchers go through hot and cold streaks. They can't pick and choose when those streaks happen, because if they could, they'd all pick to be hot in October. Derek Jeter hit .235 in the 1998 playoffs, .226 in the 2001 playoffs, .245 in 2004, .176 in 2007, and .250 in 2010 and 2011. He also had plenty of very good results in other years. That's baseball. Aaron Ashby quite literally had the greatest October by a relief pitcher in baseball history. Next year, he could be the worst pitcher on the team in the NLDS. That's baseball. Robert Gasser could be horrible next season after his dominance in this year's playoffs. That's baseball. Look at last year's Toronto Blue Jays. Ernie Clement, literally Ernie Clement, set the record for most hits in a single postseason with an incredible 30 in 73 at bats. In 2026, he was 20% worse than league average offensively, cost his team 14 runs compared to an average hitter, and had a .285 on base percentage. In the 2025 playoffs, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. had a .356 batting average on balls in play. Addison Barger was .422, Ernie Clement was .420, and George Springer .319. Predictably, the Blue Jays scored a lot of runs in October. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER In 2026, Guerrero had a .288 BABIP, Springer was .282, Clement .272, and Barger was .063 in his few games before he got hurt. Toronto finished in last place and missed the playoffs. That is also baseball. There's no predictive value from the tournament, because players do not magically become different in October. There's just a typical distribution of outcomes, particularly among good teams, that sometimes goes your way and sometimes doesn't. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD None of this means the Brewers didn't deserve to win, or weren't a good team. They absolutely did, and they absolutely are. They deserve an immense amount of credit for identifying players in the draft or international markets, as well as in trades and free agency, that they thought they could improve or would fit specific needs. But looking for some sort of explanation or path for your favorite team to follow is insane. Because while you need good players to win, you can't predict how they'll perform over a few weeks of small sample sizes. It's just...baseball. Enjoy it when your team wins, celebrate it, and understand that the inherent variability of it ensures it can't ever be broken.

articles.title: Pitcher Michael King opts out of contract, $61 million with Padres for free agency
articles.summary: King was 10th among National League starting pitchers with a 3.21 ERA and allowed 1 run in 14 innings versus the World Series champion Brewers during the NLD...
articles.body:
Starting pitcher Michael King opted out of his $32 million player option for 2027 with the San Diego Padres and will become a free agent, according to reports.

In their ranking of the top 50 free agents in Major League Baseball this offseason, Yahoo Sports' Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman placed King as the fifth-best player available and third-best starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal and Freddy Peralta.

King, who will turn 32 on May 25, compiled a 3.21 ERA this past season, ranking 10th among National League starters. He finished with a 12-10 record in 32 starts with 159 strikeouts in 185 innings.

That rate of 7.7 strikeouts per nine innings is King's lowest since becoming a full-time starting pitcher in 2024 after joining the Padres as part of the package the New York Yankees traded for Juan Soto .

King also had a strong postseason, making two starts in which he allowed 1 run with 14 strikeouts in 12 innings versus the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Division Series. The right-hander also made a relief appearance in Game 3, pitching 2 innings to earn the save in San Diego's lone win .

For his career, King has a 3.23 ERA in 143 appearances (96 starts) with a strikeout rate of 9.5 per nine frames. He pitched three seasons with the Padres, preceded by five years with the Yankees.

The eight-year veteran signed a three-year, $75 million contract last December that included opt-outs after the first two seasons. King leaves $66 million behind after choosing free agency, though he receives a $5 million buyout. Obviously, he feels he will make more on the open market amid a mediocre class of starting pitchers.

Unless King re-signs with the Padres, their starting rotation is thin as the offseason begins with Robbie Ray, Casey Mize, Lucas Giolito and Walker Buehler all free agents. Yu Darvish has two years remaining on his contract, but is considering retirement .

articles.title: Jacob Misiorowski's Hat, Ashby's Glasses & All Brewers Artifacts Added to HOF After World Series Run
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday evening.

Items from their Fall Classic run will now be donated to the National Baseball Hall of Fame, including ace pitcher Jacon Misiorowski's Game 5 hat and left-handed reliever Aaron Ashby's iconic glasses.

Top Photos From Brewers' World Series Win

Catcher (and World Series MVP) William Contreras' chest protector and shinguards

Left-handed reliever Aaron Ashby's glasses

Right fielder Sal Frelick's Game 2 batting gloves

Left fielder Christian Yelich's Game 4 jersey

Shortstop Cooper Pratt's Game 4 and 5 bat

Starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski's Game 5 cap

Second baseman Brice Turang's Game 5 cleats

All of the items are significant, of course.

Contreras was a defensive wizard behind the plate, throwing out four runners and guiding a fantastic Brewers staff that allowed just 12 runs over five games. He also fared well in his ABS challenge efforts, with 10 of his 13 calls overturned.

Manager Pat Murphy was promoted from bench coach to manager when Craig Counsell left town for the Chicago Cubs three years ago, and he's since led the Brewers to three NL Central titles and win totals of 93, 97 and 103.

This year's team was the best of all, of course, and is just one of eight teams in the past 40 years to win 100 or more regular season games and the World Series in the same year.

Ashby threw 18 scoreless innings in these playoffs, striking out 20 while allowing just five hits and three walks. Right fielder Sal Frelick hit a game-tying solo home run in Game 2 to help turn a 4-0 first-inning deficit into a 5-4 win.

Left fielder Christian Yelich, the Brewers' captain, has been with the team for nine seasons. He's made three All-Star Games and won the National League MVP in 2018.

Pratt was sensational in Games 4 and 5. He nearly was the hero in Game 4, hitting a solo homer in the top of the 12th to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead before Tampa Bay came back for a 4-3 win. That gave him four hits. Pratt then added two RBI and a run in Game 5.

Misiorowski, the presumptive National League Cy Young winner, threw 5.2 shutout innings in Game 5, putting the Brewers in an advantageous position for the series clincher.

Second baseman Brice Turang had a pair of hits (including a double) and a run in Game 5. His 100 RBI this season led the team.

articles.title: Bo Bichette Makes Decision on Mets Contract Option in New Rumors with $84M Left on Deal
articles.summary: Coming off a disappointing 2026 season, Bo Bichette is staying with the New York Mets as he looks to rebound next year.
articles.body:
Coming off a disappointing 2026 season, Bo Bichette is staying with the New York Mets as he looks to rebound next year.

Per Will Sammon of The Athletic, Bichette will opt in to his $42 million salary for the 2027 season to remain with the Mets. The infielder is also owed $42 million in 2028, but will have another chance to opt out next winter.

1 Player Every Team Must Re-Sign in Free Agency 💰

Everything to Know on Lockout and Key Upcoming Dates ⚾

One of the top free agents last offseason, Bichette signed a unique three-year, $126 million contract to join the Mets in January 2026. He has opt-outs after each of the first two seasons, potentially giving him the opportunity to secure a longer-term deal.

It seemed apparent very early in the 2026 campaign that Bichette would decide to stay with the Mets given his struggles at the plate. He hit .255/.300/.376 prior to the All-Star break.

Things did improve for Bichette after the break with a .267/.329/.411 slash line, but it was highly unlikely he would be able to get a contract on the open market anywhere close to the money he will get by opting in.

Bichette has been up and down over the past three seasons. His 2024 campaign was limited to just 81 games due to injuries, then he bounced back in 2025 with a .311/.357/.483 slash line in 139 games to help the Toronto Blue Jays win the AL East.

A knee injury kept Bichette out for the first two rounds of the playoffs, but he returned to post a .923 OPS in the World Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Despite a difficult 2026 season, Bichette and the Mets have reasons to be optimistic about a bounce back in 2027. He is only 28 and was also learning to play a new position at third base because Francisco Lindor is entrenched at shortstop in Queens.

If the Mets get the best version of Bichette next season, it will provide a huge boost as they look to get back to being a playoff contender in the NL.

articles.title: 2-time All-Star Bo Bichette reportedly opting in for $42M to return to Mets in 2027
articles.summary: With the threat of a lockout looming while coming off a relatively down season, Bichette reportedly opted for the security of a $42 million deal rather than...
articles.body:
Bo Bichette is ready to run it back with the New York Mets.

The two-time All-Star infielder intends to exercise a $42 million player option to return to the Mets for the 2027 season, The Athletic reports .

Bichette joined the Mets last offseason as one of the prized free agents in his class after seven standout seasons with the Toronto Blue Jays. He signed a three-year $126 million contract with player options for 2027 and 2028.

When he joined the Mets, they were eyeing contention for a World Series title in 2026. The Mets instead were arguably the biggest disappointment in baseball with a 74-88 record and last-place finish in the NL East.

Bichette, 28, got off to a slow start in his first season with New York, but rallied to finish with a .260/.312/.390 slash line with 18 home runs and 78 RBI. The full-season production was below the All-Star standard he set with the Blue Jays, but he flashed his former All-Star form late in the season.

With the threat of a lockout looming while coming off a relatively down season, Bichette opted for the security of a $42 million deal rather than risk going into a work stoppage without a contract. He maintains his player option for 2028 and could command more value on a longer deal next offseason if he returns to his All-Star form.

The Mets, meanwhile, are hoping Bichette can contribute to a turnaround in 2027 when and if baseball is actually played.

articles.title: Dustin May's Decision on Brewers Contract Option Revealed in New Rumors After Winning World Series
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May will become a free agent after declining his mutual option for the 2027 MLB season on Thursday, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post.
articles.body:
Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May will become a free agent after declining his mutual option for the 2027 MLB season on Thursday, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post .

The mutual option was worth $20 million (via Spotrac ).

May's decision comes one day after the Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to win the 2026 World Series, capturing their first championship in franchise history.

He opened the 2026 season with the St. Louis Cardinals before he was sent to Milwaukee in an Aug. 3 trade .

The Brewers received May and left-handed reliever JoJo Romero from St. Louis in exchange for minor league outfielders Alexander Frías and Josiah Ragsdale.

May started 21 games for the Cardinals prior to the trade, posting a 7-9 record to go along with a 4.38 ERA and 1.284 WHIP. He also recorded 106 strikeouts compared to 35 walks in 109 innings of work.

The 29-year-old's production dipped following the change of scenery, as he compiled a 5.65 ERA across 10 starts with the Brewers. Opposing batters also posted a .796 OPS against May during his time in Milwaukee.

He was primarily utilized as a bullpen piece during the Brewers' ensuing playoff run, allowing 11 hits and seven earned runs in 11 innings pitched.

Teams looking to sign May in free agency will hope that he can put his struggles in 2026 behind him, as he owned a 3.86 career ERA prior to this season.

articles.title: Baseball May NEVER See Anything Like This Again! Jackson Chourio and William Contreras Just Conquered the Entire Sport in One INSANE Season!
articles.summary: What Jackson Chourio and William Contreras have accomplished in 2026 is almost impossible to put into words. These two Milwaukee Brewers stars have experienc...
articles.body:
What Jackson Chourio and William Contreras have accomplished in 2026 is almost impossible to put into words. These two Milwaukee Brewers stars have experienced a season that most professional baseball players can only dream about, collecting championships, breaking records and dominating on the biggest stages in the sport.

And somehow, they saved their best moments for October.

It all started with the World Baseball Classic. Chourio and Contreras helped Venezuela capture its first WBC championship, giving them an international title before the MLB regular season had even begun. They would eventually add another championship to their resumes just seven months later.

The Brewers followed up their international success with an incredible regular season, finishing with 103 wins — the best record in all of baseball and a franchise record.

Chourio, at just 22 years old, put together another outstanding campaign, hitting .291 with 25 home runs, 75 RBIs, 96 runs scored and 23 stolen bases. Contreras was equally important, batting .270 with 18 home runs, 94 RBIs and 153 hits while serving as the leader behind the plate.

Milwaukee wasn't just winning games. It was building one of the most dominant teams in baseball.

The postseason started with a four-game battle against the Padres, and both players delivered.

Contreras hit .375 with two home runs, two RBIs and a 1.194 OPS across the series. His power was on full display, including a go-ahead home run in Game 1.

Chourio had a quieter series at the plate overall, hitting .188, but he came through in the biggest moment of Game 2. With Milwaukee down to its final opportunity, he delivered a walk-off two-run single to give the Brewers a 2-0 series lead.

Milwaukee eventually finished the job in Game 4, advancing with a 3-1 series victory.

Next came the defending champions, and Milwaukee made them look completely helpless.

The Brewers swept Los Angeles in four games, getting revenge for their previous postseason disappointment against the Dodgers.

Contreras continued his incredible postseason, batting .357 with five hits, a home run, three RBIs and a 1.113 OPS. His Game 2 performance was especially impressive, delivering a game-tying home run before adding another go-ahead hit as Milwaukee took control.

Chourio struggled more in this series, hitting .158 with one home run and one RBI, but his overall postseason contributions were still important to Milwaukee's championship run.

The Brewers completed the sweep with a 6-4 victory in Game 4, punching their ticket to the World Series.

This is where Chourio and Contreras put the finishing touches on an unforgettable season.

At just 22 years old, Chourio absolutely exploded against Tampa Bay. He hit .458 in the World Series, collecting 11 hits through the first four games. That tied Babe Ruth for the most hits through the first four games of a World Series.

He also became the youngest player to record a four-hit World Series game since 1946, doing it at 22 years and 229 days old. He finished the series with 11 hits, four runs scored and two RBIs.

Contreras was just as important, and his impact went far beyond the batter's box.

He hit .381 with four RBIs across the five games, including a run-scoring single in Game 1 and a crucial RBI double in the deciding Game 5. Behind the plate, he threw out four attempted base stealers and consistently controlled Tampa Bay's running game. He also won 10 of his 13 challenges using MLB's Automated Ball-Strike system.

When the final out was recorded in Milwaukee's 4-1 series victory, Contreras was named World Series MVP — becoming the first player in Brewers history to win the award.

A season that belongs in baseball history

Think about everything these two have accomplished in a single calendar year.

World Baseball Classic champions with Venezuela.

MLB's best regular-season record at 103 wins.

A National League Division Series victory over San Diego.

A four-game sweep of the defending champion Dodgers.

World Series champions after defeating Tampa Bay in five games.

William Contreras taking home World Series MVP.

Jackson Chourio making history at just 22 years old.

The Brewers finished the postseason 11-2, losing just two games on their way to the franchise's first World Series championship.

There are great seasons, there are championship seasons, and then there is what Chourio and Contreras just accomplished.

Two championships in one year, a historic regular season, record-breaking postseason moments and a World Series MVP.
